title: Grateful Dead Live at Gym, S.U.N.Y. on 1970-10-31
lineage: SBD > MR > Cass > DAT > WAV > CD Wave > SHN

ai_review.summary: Solid 1970 Halloween show with strong performances of “The Other One” and New Riders set, captured on a good‑quality soundboard recording despite some low‑volume quirks.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the high‑energy Halloween night, especially the smoky “The Other One,” tight drumming from Mickey and Bill, and the added flavor of the New Riders of the Purple Sage set. The soundboard source is generally clear and well‑balanced, though a few listeners note low guitar volume and occasional clams that hint at venue‑related issues.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating is 4.2 across ten reviews; most praise the performance and recording, with only one strongly negative review pulling the overall sentiment toward mixed.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well‑mixed “classic 1970 sound,” but some listeners note low guitar volume, occasional clams/artifacts, and overall modest fidelity compared to the best Dead recordings.

poor_songs: Good Lovin' (later section considered drum‑heavy and weaker)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Halloween vibe with a slow start on “St. Stephen,” building into tighter jams; the inclusion of the New Riders set adds continuity to the night, giving listeners the feel of a full GD/NRPS experience.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone and chord voicings are highlighted as complex and evolving; his licks are praised even amid low volume concerns.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh is noted for fitting nicely with Jerry, providing a solid bass foundation.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann lock in tightly on “Good Lovin'” and deliver fantastic drumming on “The Other One,” though later portions of “Good Lovin'” are criticized as overly drum‑focused.
